findings.assessment: All string pointers are initialized before any failure path; each malloc/scanf failure either owns nothing or calls the common cleanup. size=0 still permits malloc(0) returning NULL. Valid input behavior is preserved.
Both string pointers receive malloc results before the joint test; freeModel may safely free either NULL and releases the surviving allocation. The helper no longer calls strcpy on NULL.
Same allocation-failure correction as the previous independent example; it preserves pointers to make and id and runs them only after successful allocation.

The revised union explanation distinguishes permitted scalar lifetime start from assignment to an inactive std::string and notes that the old member is not automatically destroyed. It corrects a materially false general rule.

Ints was first defined only in the following step, whereas the preceding step defines Floats. Adding the existing intended definition makes this fragment usable at its actual position; field types match the subsequent example.

A copy of the shared_ptr root shares mutable nodes while keeping two separate root handles. Rotations through the copied owner can make original keys unreachable. Deleting copy construction/assignment is a minimal ownership policy; implicit move is unavailable too. No current course usage requires copying this tree.

The example is intentionally invalid because Display is incomplete at the friend member declaration. The old missing class boundary introduced a second unrelated syntax error; the patch restores Display while preserving the intended failure.

Default card construction now initializes both fields. Invalid or failed position input exits before selected-card comparison. Valid positions 1--3 retain behavior. Added clocale supplies the declared setlocale dependency.

Unbounded strcpy into char[20]/char[40] had no documented length precondition. std::string preserves complete names; every affected printf %s receives c_str(). The virtual price base and price calculation are unchanged.

An abstract base may contain virtual implementations inherited by a concrete derived class. The prior assertion that only nonvirtual elements are inherited was false. The replacement preserves the abstract-instantiation restriction.
